note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
In the epistle to Philemon, Epaphras shows up again: “There salute thee Epaphras, my fellowprisoner in Christ Jesus.” Paul calls Epaphras his fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus. But why is he mentioned in the letter to Philemon? Because Philemon was also of Colosse.

“Marcus, Aristarchus, Demas, Lucas, my fellowlabourers.” Remember Demas: when you read Timothy, Demas forsook this truth. “The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.”

The letters Paul wrote from Rome to that region, Ephesians, Colossians and Philemon, overlap and name the same people because he wrote them at the same time and to the same place. Following Epaphras through them shows how the work in Colosse spread from one faithful brother to a whole company of labourers.

precepts.text: Paul writes unto Philemon our dearly beloved, and fellowlabourer, and to the church in thy house. It started with Epaphras, then you had others come.
precepts.point: Epaphras was a self-starter. He did not need someone right there to get the ground running. He heard the truth, believed it, and went and taught it.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
“Paul, a prisoner of Jesus Christ, and Timothy our brother, unto Philemon our dearly beloved, and fellowlabourer, And to our beloved Apphia, and Archippus our fellowsoldier, and to the church in thy house.”

Philemon was of Colosse, the same place Epaphras taught. So it started with Epaphras, and then others came: Philemon, a dearly beloved fellow labourer, Apphia, Archippus the fellow soldier, and a church meeting in Philemon’s house.

That is how the truth spreads. One brother, a faithful minister of Christ, wakes up and teaches, and then fellow labourers rise up around him and congregations meet in houses, the same way schools pop up one after another today.

precepts.text: I beseech thee for my son Onesimus, whom I have begotten in my bonds. Why would Paul say that to Philemon? Because they had to be in the same place: Colosse.
precepts.point: Epaphras was a self-starter. He did not need someone right there to get the ground running. He heard the truth, believed it, and went and taught it.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
“I beseech thee for my son Onesimus, whom I have begotten in my bonds.” Why would Paul write to Philemon on behalf of Onesimus? Because they had to be in the same place: Colosse.

Colossians 4:9 calls Onesimus “a faithful and beloved brother, who is one of you,” one of the Colossians. And he is the same Onesimus Paul begot in his bonds and sent back to Philemon.

So the letters tie together. Epaphras, Philemon and Onesimus all belong to Colosse, and the epistles to the Colossians and to Philemon were carried to the same city, to the same congregation of Israelites that had learned the truth of Epaphras.
